comment: The bare-`case` discriminator fabrication, pinned in BOTH directions. POSITIVE: a genuine `case kind: Kind` discriminator is a real field of its object, so `kind` is published as a property with its `contains` edge — a one-sided pin could be satisfied by dropping every discriminator in the language, and this half is what forbids that. NEGATIVE: on the bare `case` form, tree-sitter-nim's error recovery attaches the following `of A, B:` line to the discriminator slot, and the analyzer must not publish the borrowed names. Four distinct borrowed spellings are pinned, chosen because each defeats a different cheap guard: `AddOpr` and `SubOpr` are legal identifiers, not keywords, so a reserved-word list misses them; `None` is the single-branch shape from nimony/lib/std/opt.nim:34; `float` is a field's TYPE name, recovered from further away in nimony/tests/nimony/object/tsumtype_shared.nim:9, and defeats both a keyword list and a 'is it a constructor of this variant' test. The `contains` forbids are the half that catches a fix which routes the borrowed name through a different owner field.

expectSymbols.name: kind
expectSymbols.comment: POSITIVE. A genuine discriminator is written adjacent to `case`, so this IS a field of Tagged. The guard is scoped to the bare form and must not cost this row.

expectSymbols.name: Node
expectSymbols.comment: published, but with NO fields: on the bare form every branch name is a constructor

expectRelationships.comment: POSITIVE, and the specific row a blanket suppression of `variant_discriminator_declaration` would delete

forbidSymbols.name: AddOpr
forbidSymbols.comment: the first constructor of the absorbed `of AddOpr, SubOpr:` line. Not a Nim reserved word, so a keyword-list guard misses it. Published as `property AddOpr` on Node with a `contains` edge before the guard — 2 edges at nimony/tests/nimony/object/deps/msumtype.nim:4

forbidSymbols.name: SubOpr
forbidSymbols.comment: the second constructor of the same absorbed line — pinned separately because the guard reads the slot's FIRST declaration, so a bug that reads only the first name could still leak the rest

forbidSymbols.name: None
forbidSymbols.comment: the single-branch bare form, from nimony/lib/std/opt.nim:34. 6 edges pointed at it there, the largest single payload of this defect in that repo

forbidSymbols.name: Some
forbidSymbols.comment: the second branch of the same single-branch variant

forbidSymbols.name: float
forbidSymbols.comment: THE HARD ONE. Recovered from further away — a field's TYPE name, not a branch name (nimony/tests/nimony/object/tsumtype_shared.nim:9 published `property float` on Shape). Defeats a reserved-word guard AND a 'name is one of this variant's constructors' guard, which is why the shipped rule tests the `case`-row adjacency instead. This forbid is what stops a future 'cheap' rewrite of the guard.

forbidSymbols.name: Circle
forbidSymbols.comment: the branch name of the bare `case` inside Shape. The case with ONE branch, where recovery lands on the constructor

forbidRelationships.comment: the fabricated edge itself. The object Node has no field AddOpr; the graph must not assert one
the shape that defeats a keyword guard, asserted as an edge as well as a symbol so a fix that routes the name through a different owner is caught
the opt.nim:34 payload. `Opt` is deliberately not in expectSymbols — the point of this forbid is that the edge may not exist whether or not the owner was published
